chunks: So give them news of painful punishment,
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran mean by 'painful punishment' in the context of giving glad tidings?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Inshiqaq is often contextualized within the broader narrative of divine retribution against those who persist in rejecting the truth despite clear signs, echoing the fate of earlier nations. It serves not merely as a threat but as a confirmation of the inevitability of the Hereafter, reinforcing the concept of 'Adl' (Divine Justice) where punishment is a direct consequence of free-will rejection. The 'painful punishment' is interpreted by scholars like Allamah Tabatabai as encompassing both the spiritual anguish of regret and the physical torment of the grave and resurrection.
